headline: Ship an AI agent portfolio piece this quarter — founders who own the agentic stack will outpace the competition in 2026.
why_now: GitHub activity (96) and project potential (96) are at near-peak levels, signaling the ecosystem is exploding with reusable patterns. Hugging Face activity (92) and news mentions (88) confirm both tooling and public attention are there. For a founder building a portfolio, this is the rare window where a single well-documented agent project can carry disproportionate credibility.
study: Spend 3 days on Anthropic's agent loop docs and LangChain's ReAct/Plan-and-Execute guides to internalize the planning-tool-memory pattern.
Build 5 throwaway agents in the LangGraph or CrewAI playground (web scraper, API orchestrator, code reviewer, research assistant, calendar bot) to feel tool-calling and error recovery.
Read 3 production agent repos on GitHub (e.g., LangChain's open-source multi-agent demos) and reverse-engineer their prompts, memory schemas, and fallback handling.
Study evaluation: 1 day on TruLens, LangSmith, or Braintrust so your portfolio project shows observability, not just a demo.

build.title: AgentOS — an open-source 'operating system' for solo founders that plans, executes, and logs multi-step workflows across email, CRM, and docs
build.description: A LangGraph/CrewAI agent with a planner node, specialized worker agents (inbox triage, follow-up drafter, meeting prep, research), shared vector memory, and an eval dashboard. It impresses because it tackles a real founder pain (context-switching) with the full agentic pattern — planning, tool use, multi-agent collaboration, and self-critique — instead of a toy demo.
deliverables: Public GitHub repo with clean architecture diagram, ADR (architecture decision record), and one-command Docker setup
Live demo deployed on Vercel/Railway with a sandbox dataset and a 60-second Loom walkthrough
Technical write-up on your blog or Dev.to covering the agent graph, failure modes, and eval results
Short README GIF showing the planner decomposing a real founder task end-to-end

publish: Post the demo on Product Hunt and Hacker News (Show HN) with a 'Show: AgentOS — open-source agent OS for founders' headline on a Tuesday or Wednesday morning.
Share a 5-tweet thread with architecture screenshots tagging LangChain, LangGraph, and a founder community like Lenny's Newsletter readers.
Submit a 4-minute talk proposal to AI Engineer World's Fair, LangChain's meetups, or a local AI meetup — speakers get 10x the inbound of lurkers.
Cross-post the write-up to Indie Hackers, Reddit r/LocalLLaMA, and r/MachineLearning with a results-first summary.
risks: API cost surprises during demos — a runaway agent loop can burn through budget; cap iterations and set hard token limits.
Over-engineering the agent graph before validating the user problem — start with a 3-node linear flow and add branching only after a real user tests it.
Demo rot: APIs and SDK versions shift weekly in this space; lock dependency versions in the README and add a 'last tested' badge so reviewers trust it still works.
confidence: Very high — signals across code, model hubs, news, and hiring all point the same direction, and the build target is a tangible artifact a founder can demo in interviews and to investors.
